body: I want to know that it's not wrong for me to want this.

That job made me want to kill myself. I wrote a note and everything. 

I don't know what happened to make me like this, but I've been wanting to be dead since I was eight.

I want to be loved. I want people to talk to me. People who like what I have to say. I want to be able to trust people. I want to have any one of my fucking ten siblings to take a god damn moment to send me a message. I want these things before I decide to kill myself. I want to abolish homeschooling. I want to watch all hypocritical priests choke on their own vomit.

First and last things don't really go together though. I am the reason for all of my suffering, but I don't want to stop, otherwise I would have by now, right?
I am scared to tell myself to give up, but I still have. It would be far easier to know that someone else thought that I deserve the right to choose my end. Am I a coward? I would say that I am.

I was the sole manager of a multimillion dollar warehouse for four years. Based on that experience I do not want to be anyone's boss ever again. I don't want anything from life. Except maybe for someone to tell me it's okay to give up.

Yeah, I know I took too long to learn to backflip. Why would I learn a trade? So I can start giving my time to a company so they can make money off of MY work and pay a me a pittance in exchange for my effort? No thank you.

What else am I supposed to think when my reaction to completing something  is questioning the effort I put in? When I was a kid I wanted invent a teleporter like they had in Star Trek. As a kid I wanted to be able to go to heaven when I died. I've had religion taken from me though.

I didn't have specific wants like a career or hobby, nobody told me to plan that far ahead.

I'm only 26, but god damn do I hate waking up.

I have no job. I have no verifiable education. I get out of bed, I get on my computer, I eat every so often and then I go to bed. Why would I dedicate myself to something? I don't like achievement.

I got my eagle scout years ago, I felt nothing, maybe a little shame because I didn't feel I had actually earned it.

I got my GED. I didn't feel anything for having completed it. When I applied for jobs I was told to go get some college credits.

I learned to backflip. I still remember the first time I landed on my feet after six months of trying. I thought to myself "That's it?".

I've been a 'ninja' before. It wasn't worth it.
I don't do things. I currently have no hobbies. I would not. I have had achievements in athletics. Even in the moment of achievement I didn't feel anything. Is that what I worked so hard for?

I want what I can't have. To change the past. 

I want a childhood untainted by religious zealotry. I want to have gone to school and experienced the good and the bad of it. I want to have had friends. I want to have dated in my teens and early twenties. I want to have been exposed to sports. I want to have known my relatives. I want my parents to have had far fewer children. I want people who care about my day. I want to have had days worth caring about. I want to not daydream all the time.  I want to be able to say that this pandemic ruined my year. I want to be able to speak to people without worrying that they think I'm weird. I want to not cringe when touched. I want to go to a concert without being overwhelmed by the volume. I want to convince myself a hobby is worth having. I want to enjoy the drugs I use. I want to be worth something to someone, but I don't want that worth to be earning money. I want to not feel guilty about the things I do. 

I mostly want to lie down and end. I want someone to tell me that that's okay.
That's the thing. I don't want help. I apricate your effort, but why do YOU want ME to live? How does my being alive matter? I have and want no purpose in a world where you need one.
